mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in more than 40% of instances following a FEDFUNDS increase > 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% in a single month indicates a weakening economy, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 60% of the cases following a sharp increase in UNRATE.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real estate sales (HOUST) over three consecutive months signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 55% of the cases following a sustained decline in HOUST.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in a single month signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the cases following a significant increase in INDPRO.

mechanism_narrative: When real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) grow faster than the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) over a three-month period, it indicates strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS growth > CPIAUCSL growth over 3 months
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the cases following a period where RSAFS growth exceeds CPIAUCSL growth.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 100,000 in a single month signals a weakening labor market, which historically correlates with negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 60% of the cases following a significant decrease in PAYEMS.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it signals an inflationary environment with accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the cases following the described trigger conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a strengthening economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and consumer spending improve.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 55% of the cases following a sustained increase in GDPC1.
